title: How an SWP works
objectives: Explain an SWP and what each withdrawal is.
Say what an SWP does not guarantee, and what to refer to a CA.
body_md:
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount from a fund at set intervals, usually monthly. Each withdrawal is a redemption of units, so: only the gains part of each withdrawal is a capital gain; the rest is the investor's own money coming back. Tax depends on the fund type and holding period; refer the client to a CA. Exit loads can apply to units within the exit-load period. An SWP does not guarantee income. If returns are lower than withdrawals for long, the corpus shrinks.

> **Investor takeaway:** An SWP is a withdrawal plan, not guaranteed income.
example: Monthly SWP of ₹40,000 from a liquid fund: each payout redeems units; only the gains part is a capital gain.
say: Only the gains part of each withdrawal is a capital gain.
An SWP does not guarantee income.
never: The whole SWP withdrawal is taxed as gains.
An SWP is a guaranteed pension.

check.why: Redeems a fixed amount regularly. It is a withdrawal plan, not guaranteed income.

check.q: Is the whole SWP withdrawal taxed as capital gains?
check.why: No, only the gains part. Refer details to a CA.
